name: MySQL NDB Cluster
tagline: Shared-nothing, auto-sharded in-memory MySQL engine built for telecom-grade availability.
description: MySQL NDB Cluster pairs MySQL Server front ends with NDB, a distributed shared-nothing storage engine originally built at Ericsson for telecom subscriber databases. Data is automatically partitioned across data nodes and synchronously replicated within node groups, giving five-nines availability, online scaling and sub-millisecond primary-key access, with disk-backed tables for colder data. Beyond SQL it exposes NoSQL-style APIs (NDB API, ClusterJ, Node.js adapter) that bypass the SQL layer. It shines for HLR/5G, gaming and session state, but its join performance, operational complexity and differences from InnoDB make it a specialist tool.

pricing.notes: Community edition under GPLv2; MySQL Cluster Carrier Grade Edition is a commercial Oracle subscription.

scale.notes: Up to 144 data nodes; automatic sharding by primary key hash. Geo-replication between clusters with conflict detection.

strengths: Automatic sharding and synchronous replication with no single point of failure
Sub-millisecond primary-key reads and writes from memory
Online add-node, rolling upgrades and online schema changes
Direct NDB API access for millions of ops/sec without SQL parsing
weaknesses: Joins and range scans across data nodes are much slower than InnoDB
Different semantics from InnoDB (READ COMMITTED only, size limits per row)
Operationally complex: management, data and SQL nodes to size and tune
Memory-resident by default, so large datasets get expensive
useCases: Session and user-profile stores needing five-nines uptime
Payment authorization with strict availability SLAs
notIdealFor: Small teams without dedicated DBA time
